remaining_gaps: The end is EO 10903 Sec. 5(a)(3) (26 FR 217, signed 1961-01-09), whose Federal Register text is held (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10903.txt) but whose acting provision is not located as a packet evidence record (dossier missing line "target provision not located: EO:10903"), so it is not citable; it needs an independently reviewed act-override or source supplement. The effective date of that revocation also depends on the Sec. 5(b) savings and the regulations the order contemplated, and the later amendments of Sec. 1(d) by EO 10187, 10313 and 10391 are strike-and-insert events that need before-and-after text.

Sec. 7 makes the order effective on July 1, 1957, or on a later date when funds appropriated for the National Security Council became available; no held source shows which date applied, and Sec. 3(b) directs transfers of Operations Coordinating Board staff whose performance date is also not held. EO 10920 (1961-02-18) revokes the order by name, but the start date and one-time transfers need held evidence, and EO 10838 amends section 1(b).

Sec. 5 of the order directs transfer of records, property, personnel and funds of the Telecommunications Advisor to the Office of Defense Mobilization, and no held source shows whether or when that transfer was performed; without it the clause cannot be dated as exhausted by performance, and the 1962-02-16 revocation by EO 10995 Sec. 4 would not show first cessation. A held record of the transfer (agency order, budget document or Federal Register notice) is needed.

The order is revoked by Sec. 3 of EO 11012 (27 FR 2983, signed 1962-03-27), but only "effective as of that date", meaning the date on which the initial regulations issued by the Director of the Bureau of the Budget and by the Administrator of General Services under that order became effective. No held source states that date: the Bureau of the Budget regulations issued under EO 11012 (the Standardized Government Travel Regulations revision or circular) and the General Services Administration commuted-rate regulations, or a Federal Register notice of their effective dates, are not in the repository, so the first-end date of every clause cannot be fixed.

Sec. 7 of the order abolishes the Federal Development Planning Committee and revokes EO 11186 effective "on the date of the first meeting of the Commission"; no held source gives the date of the first meeting of the Appalachian Regional Commission, so that clause's exact first-end date cannot be fixed (the order itself was abolished and revoked by EO 11386, 1967-12-28, whose ACT evidence also reads as both whole and partial). A held record of the Commission's first meeting is needed.
